takeaway: Use tidal volumes of 4–8 mL/kg predicted body weight, and prone patients with PaO2/FiO2 under 150 mmHg despite PEEP of at least 5 cmH2O for sessions of at least 16 hours [1].
clinicalQuestion: Which ventilation strategy does ESICM recommend for severe ARDS?
background: Traditional ventilation aimed to normalise blood gases. ESICM prioritises limiting ventilator-induced lung injury [1].
population: Adults with ARDS, including moderate-severe disease defined by PaO2/FiO2 under 150 mmHg.
intervention: Low tidal volume and prone positioning.
comparator: Larger tidal volumes and supine ventilation.
mainFindings: Recommend low tidal volume ventilation (4–8 mL/kg predicted body weight) rather than larger volumes used to normalise blood gases, to reduce mortality in non-COVID ARDS. Strong recommendation based on expert opinion despite lack of statistical significance; high level of evidence. Recommend prone rather than supine position for moderate-severe ARDS (PaO2/FiO2 under 150 mmHg and PEEP at least 5 cmH2O after optimisation) to reduce mortality. Strong recommendation, high level of evidence; the same recommendation applies to COVID-19 ARDS with moderate evidence because of indirectness. Start prone positioning early after stabilisation on low tidal volume and adjusted PEEP if PaO2/FiO2 remains under 150, for at least 16 consecutive hours [1].
clinicalMeaning: Severe ARDS ventilation is lung-protective volume plus prolonged prone sessions, not normalisation of carbon dioxide at the cost of large volumes [1].
limitations: The low-tidal-volume recommendation notes a lack of statistical significance even though the panel still makes a strong recommendation. COVID-19 evidence is downgraded for indirectness [1].
bottomLine: Set 4–8 mL/kg predicted body weight and, if PaO2/FiO2 stays under 150 on PEEP of at least 5, prone for 16 hours or more [1].
practiceImplication: Do not delay proning until late refractory hypoxaemia once the PaO2/FiO2 criterion is met after stabilisation [1].
trustRationale: Current ESICM guideline with explicit recommendation strength.
whatNotToOverclaim: A near-drowning ECMO case is not the ventilation recommendation.
